title: Distributional Effects of Tariffs
summary: Yale Budget Lab panel of tax economists on who bears the tariff burden: tariffs are a regressive tax on Americans whose price-level effect depends on the Fed.

assertions.quote: it's up to them to decide which of these two costs that we um we bear

verdicts.note: A tariff is an indirect tax whose wedge is resolved through higher prices or lower nominal incomes, and monetary policy determines which; in 2025 the Fed chose to look through it.

assertions.quote: first and foremost you know these are taxes on Americans
the burden is uh larger as a share of income for lower inome households uh than higher inome households

verdicts.note: Lower-income households spend a larger share of income, and more of it on traded goods, so distributional analyses of broad tariffs consistently find a regressive burden.

assertions.quote: That makes manufacturing in the United States harder, not easier if you're making our input goods more expensive.

verdicts.note: The 2018 steel and aluminum tariffs measurably raised input costs and reduced employment in downstream manufacturing.

assertions.quote: the sort of burden can can be larger than the revenue

verdicts.note: Tariffs create deadweight loss as buyers substitute toward pricier domestic goods, so estimated consumer costs exceeded collected revenue in studies of the 2018 tariffs.

assertions.quote: You're either going to see a fall in factor incomes, wages or capital income, or you're going to see a rise in um consumer prices.

verdicts.note: Standard tax incidence: the tariff wedge lowers real purchasing power either through prices or through factor incomes.

assertions.quote: countries that try to raise a significant amount of revenue from tariffs have less efficient economies

verdicts.note: Trade theory and cross-country experience show tariff-reliant economies protect low-productivity sectors; no rich country raises significant revenue from tariffs.

assertions.quote: If you're cutting an income tax and you're expanding a consumption tax, that's going to be a regressive move.

verdicts.note: The US income tax is strongly progressive while a tariff burden is roughly proportional to consumption, so the swap shifts burden down the income scale.

assertions.quote: many transfer programs are indexed on inflation

verdicts.note: Social Security, SNAP and similar benefits adjust with the CPI, offsetting part of a tariff-driven price rise for recipients, with a lag.
